successors.name: Xianbei confederation
successors.text: the Mongolian plateau east of the Altai, left when the Northern chanyu fled west in 91 and 'most of them being absorbed by the Xianbei'

successors.name: Yueban
successors.text: the 200,000 'veterans and wounded' left in Dzungaria who 'later moved northwest to the Kazakhstan steppe and became known as the Yueban'

ledger.x: 209 BCE: Modu kills Touman and makes himself chanyu.
208 BCE: the Donghu are destroyed.
208 BCE: the rest of the Donghu country.

c. 203 BCE: Modu retakes the Ordos that Meng Tian took in 215 BCE. The Xiongnu page says Modu 'retook the original homeland of Xiongnu on the Yellow River' but gives no year, and neither the Modu Chanyu page nor the Meng Tian page (opened for this revision; it says only that the Qin collapsed 'three years after his…
203 BCE: the Xiongnu seize a large part of the Yuezhi land.
178 BCE: the Tarim passes from the Yuezhi to the Xiongnu.
178 BCE: the Xiongnu overrun the Tarim.

c. 178 BCE: the westward growth beyond the oases. Between its 197 and 170 BCE shapes Cliopatria adds 0.89 M km2: 0.36 M km2 are the Tarim and Turfan-Hami (the two events above and below) and 0.53 M km2 (Dzungaria 0.34, the Altai and upper Irtysh 0.18) are pasture that no page opened names. The Modu Chanyu page gives…
176 BCE: the Xiongnu drive the Yuezhi from the Hexi Corridor, ending the contest that began in 203.
176 BCE: the Yuezhi are driven from the Hexi Corridor.
132 BCE: the Wusun, Xiongnu vassals, take the Ili.
127 BCE: Wei Qing retakes the Ordos for Han.
124 BCE: Han armies push into the steppe.
121 BCE: Huo Qubing takes the Hexi Corridor.
121 BCE: the Wuhuan leave Xiongnu rule and the eastern grasslands are dropped.
119 BCE: the Battle of Mobei (January-June) ends the fight for the land south of the Gobi.
119 BCE: the Xiongnu court is driven north of the Gobi.

c. 115 BCE at the latest: the Wusun break with the Xiongnu. 'When the Xiongnu ruler died, Liejiaomi refused to serve the Xiongnu. The Xiongnu then sent a force against the Wusun but were defeated' (undated); the Wusun 'subsequently took over the Ili Valley, expanding over a large area and trying to keep away from the…
72 BCE: the Han-Wusun campaign.
67 BCE: Han takes Turfan.
60 BCE: the Rizhu King surrenders and the Tarim passes to Han.
60 BCE: the Protectorate of the Western Regions ends the fight for the Tarim and the west.
56 BCE: Hutuwusi revolts as Zhizhi Chanyu.
53 BCE: Huhanye submits to Han.
49 BCE: Zhizhi abandons the Orkhon for the north-west.
49 BCE: the Siberian north goes to Zhizhi.
10 CE: Wang Mang's Xin breaks with the Xiongnu.

c. 23 CE: the Xiongnu regain the Western Regions. 'The Xiongnu had taken advantage of the situation and gained control over the Western Regions'; the protector-general's post 'was abandoned' in 8-22 CE and the eighteen states asked in vain for its return in 45 CE…
48 CE: the Southern Xiongnu secede.
73 CE: Dou Gu's expedition reaches Lake Barkol.
74 CE: Han retakes Turfan.
77 CE: Han withdraws from Hami.
87 CE: the Xianbei kill the chanyu.
June 89: Dou Xian's expedition.
91: the Xianbei war ends with the Northern chanyu's flight.
91: Han re-establishes Hami and the protectorate.
91: the plateau passes to the Xianbei.
February 91: the last Han pursuit.
94: Fenghou is acclaimed chanyu of the remnant.
119: the remnants capture Yiwu.
126: Ban Yong subjugates the remnants.
151: the Huyan King, last of the Northern Xiongnu, is driven from Yiwu and disappears from the record.

wars.name: Xiongnu conquest of the Donghu
wars.outcome: Xiongnu victory: 'By 208 BCE, the Donghu had been defeated'; the remnants became the Xianbei and Wuhuan.

wars.name: Xiongnu–Yuezhi wars
wars.outcome: Xiongnu victory: the Yuezhi defeated in 203 BCE, overrun in 178 BCE, driven from Hexi in 176 BCE with their king killed; the Wusun became Xiongnu vassals.

wars.name: Battle of Baideng
wars.outcome: Xiongnu victory without territorial change: Gaozu besieged at Baideng (Datong) in the winter of 200 BCE; the heqin treaty of 198 BCE gave the chanyu a Han princess and gifts with 'equal status, and a boundary wall', renewed nine times to 135 BCE.

wars.name: Han–Xiongnu War
wars.outcome: Han victory: 'Establishment of Han suzerainty in the Western Regions'; the Ordos (127 BCE), Hexi (121 BCE) and the Tarim (60 BCE) lost, the chanyu driven north of the Gobi (119 BCE), Huhanye a Han tributary (53 BCE), the Southern Xiongnu Han vassals (50 CE)…

wars.name: Xiongnu civil war of the five chanyus
wars.outcome: Huhanye prevails with Han support after submitting in 53 BCE; Zhizhi takes the north-west in 49 BCE, moves to Kangju in 44 BCE and is killed at the Battle of Zhizhi in 36 BCE.

wars.name: Xianbei–Northern Xiongnu war
wars.outcome: Xianbei victory: chanyu Youliu killed in 87; after the Han campaigns of 89-91 the scattered Northern Xiongnu were 'absorbed by the Xianbei' and the plateau passed to them.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout; the one sharp line is the Han frontier along the Qin and Han walls ('a boundary wall' in the 198 BCE heqin terms), and the Hexi and Ordos commandery borders after 127-111 BCE belong to the Han dossier.
